claims.text: The FeCoNiCrAl feedstock has a particle-size range of 15–45 μm.
Bond coats made from the 15–45 μm feedstock using standard carrier gases fall short of the required coating thickness.
Helium enrichment will enhance feedstock-particle heating during thermal spraying.
Helium enrichment will increase feedstock-particle acceleration and kinetic energy.
Enhanced heating will cause a larger fraction of FeCoNiCrAl particles to become fully molten.
Greater particle melting and kinetic energy will produce denser splats.
Greater particle melting and kinetic energy will improve splat adhesion.
Denser, better-adhered splats will increase deposition efficiency and coating build-up.
Helium has higher thermal conductivity than the standard carrier gases considered.
Helium has lower atomic mass than the standard carrier gases considered.
Helium enrichment will reduce particle residence time in the high-temperature flame.
Reduced residence time in the flame will reduce oxidative exposure and preserve alloy integrity.
The helium-enriched process will produce a thicker coating than the standard-carrier-gas baseline.
The helium-enriched process will produce a bond coat that meets or exceeds the required thickness.
The helium-enriched coating will have microstructural integrity comparable to the baseline coating.
The helium-enriched coating will have oxidation levels comparable to the baseline coating.
The intervention should remain effective with 15–45 μm feedstock, substrate preheating of approximately 100–150 °C, and otherwise maintained spray parameters.
The resulting bond coat should remain suitable under high-temperature cyclic TBC service conditions.
Excessive helium enrichment could alter plasma characteristics and introduce coating defects.

contradictions.description: The 15–45 μm interval is defined as the feedstock particle-size range, but the falsification rule treats that same interval as though it were the baseline coating-thickness range. No baseline coating-thickness range is actually provided.
